leads.summary: The background catch-up also sends a browsing calendar back to today's month
leads.consequence: If the calendar is open on a different month when a clock step or resume leaves the displayed minute stale, the five-second timer calls root.refresh(). That method unconditionally invokes the loaded (though normally invisible) popup's refresh(), whose goToToday() overwrites the user's chosen viewYear/viewMonth. An open popup jumps back to the current month, even though updating the bar label did not require changing the calendar's navigation. The existing Panel.qml SystemClock:230-234 explicitly preserves a non-current month on ordinary ticks; limit this background path to the label or add a non-navigating panel date update. Source-derived, not GUI reproduced.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4; published as optional note (source only)

leads.summary: Existing locally cloned clocks do not receive this fix
leads.consequence: A user who ran `omarchy plugin clone omarchy.clock` before this upgrade uses a copied BarWidget.qml and Model.js under ~/.config/omarchy/plugins, with the clone substituted for the built-in widget. The PR adds its Timer and helper only to the built-in. That user's active bar keeps the previous suspend-lag behavior until they manually reconcile their clone with the new plugin files or return to the built-in. Updating an existing clone in place would overwrite edits, so document the limitation and a safe manual merge path rather than silently replacing it. Source-derived, not reproduced with a pre-upgrade home directory.
leads.triage: dropped: verified bin/omarchy-plugin-clone copies plugins by design; applies to every change to a clonable plugin, not specific to this PR

leads.summary: The new wiring assertion passes when the entire correction timer is commented out
leads.consequence: The test reads raw `clockWidget` while the older wiring tests read a comments-stripped `widgetSource`; a QML `/* ... */` around the entire Timer block leaves the new regex true, with no active timer. Sandbox tests also pass with interval:60000 (up to one minute before checking) and repeat:false (only checks once). In each disposable mutant the actual clock test exited 0 and printed 'ok - clock checks for a stale minute and refreshes the label'. Strip both block comments and line comments before the timer assertion (the existing widgetSource strips only full-line `//` comments), assert interval:5000 and repeat:true, and preferably add a real QML timer test when a compositor is allocated.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published in More findings with Opus reproducer

leads.summary: The other open resynchronization PRs would make the extra per-clock poller redundant
leads.consequence: Both other PRs independently add a once-per-second shared Wallclock watchdog and a per-clock onJumped SystemClock resync on the same widget; if either is merged with this PR, it performs the wall-time repair immediately while this PR still schedules another 12 checks a minute for each minute-format bar clock. This is an integration/resource lead, not a claim of double label refresh: after the other handler updates the clock, the new predicate normally sees the current minute. Both other PRs currently show GitHub CONFLICTING and also have an existing qmldir conflict with the current base, not introduced by #13541; resolve that separately and select one correction strategy if combining. No QML merged execution was performed.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** While the machine is awake, the new poll can put the label back to the previous minute for about 5 seconds.

### The poll can undo SystemClock's minute tick

SystemClock's minute timer fires on a whole second of the monotonic clock, which is offset from wall-clock seconds, and it snaps to the minute when within 500 ms, so the label often turns up to half a second before the wall clock does. `clockMinuteIsStale` uses `!==`, so a poll in that gap sees the label as stale, and `refresh()` writes the previous minute back until the next poll. On Qt 6.11.2 with Quickshell's `clock.cpp` this repeated at every minute once the poll's timing lined up with the tick.

**Suggested change:** Treat a label less than 1 s ahead of `now` as current, or detect the wall-clock jump and restart SystemClock (`enabled = false; enabled = true`).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 4309fba)</summary>

# Reproducer: the catch-up poll can put the label back a minute

Reviewed head: 4309fba052e951177628ba25e8546ff467d92b38

## 1. Test case in the PR's style

Added to `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` inside the `run_node_test` block (the
PR's own cases are unchanged):

```js
// SystemClock's minute tick is a QTimer of 20 s or more, which Qt runs as a
// whole-second timer, and SystemClock snaps to the minute when the tick lands
// within 500 ms of it. So the label can turn up to half a second before the
// wall clock does. A poll in that gap must not roll it back.
assert(!calendar.clockMinuteIsStale(new Date(2026, 8, 27, 14, 6, 0), new Date(2026, 8, 27, 14, 5, 59, 700)), 'clock leaves a label SystemClock published just before the minute turned')
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (`bash test/shell.d/clock-test.sh`, exit 1):

```
not ok - clock leaves a label SystemClock published just before the minute turned
```

With `clockMinuteIsStale` returning `true` here, the Timer calls
`root.refresh()`, which sets `displayDate = new Date()`, a time that is still in
the previous minute.

## 2. Real Qt run

Setup: Qt 6.11.2, a headless `QCoreApplication` (no window). It uses Quickshell's
`SystemClock` (`src/core/clock.cpp` and `clock.hpp` from v0.3.1, unchanged) and a
QML object that copies the widget's `displayDate`, `refresh()`, `SystemClock`
handler and the PR's `Timer` with the PR's `Model.js`. Differences: logging, a
chosen Timer start time, no calendar panel, and a fixed minute format (HH:mm). `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` was offset in a
private time namespace so that monotonic minus wall time is 450 ms mod 1 s, one
possible state after any boot or resume. Times are in ms from the wall-clock
minute:

```
  -445  systemclock date=04:24:00.000      label=04:24
  -349  poll stale=true                    label=04:24
  -348  label-changed                      label=04:23
  -348  refresh                            label=04:23
 +4652  poll stale=true                    label=04:23
 +4652  label-changed                      label=04:24
 +4652  refresh                            label=04:24
```

The same sequence repeated at the next minute (−445 / −349 / +4652). The label
shows the previous minute until 4.65 s after the minute has changed.

A poll that fires in the same millisecond as SystemClock's tick, just after it
(Qt's coarse rounding moves both to the same whole monotonic second), does the
same thing:

```
  -445  systemclock date=04:24:00.000      label=04:24
  -445  poll stale=true                    label=04:24
  -445  label-changed                      label=04:23
 +4555  label-changed                      label=04:24
```

Controls from the same run:
- SystemClock without the PR's Timer published the minute 390–394 ms early,
  with no rollback. The early tick is SystemClock's own behaviour, and it is
  harmless on its own.
- The same poll timing with the helper changed to ignore a label that is less
  than 1 s ahead: `poll stale=false`, no rollback.
- A poll 1.5 s after the tick: no rollback.

Sweep: at a 250 ms phase, 1 of 20 poll timings (250 ms steps across the 5 s
period) rolled the label back, at every minute boundary of the run
(3 of 3). The run ended before the third recovered; the other two were right
again 4756 ms after the minute. At a 750 ms phase,
SystemClock ticked about 252 ms late from the second minute on: 0 of 20 timings rolled back, and 1 of 20
caused an extra `refresh()`.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

#### The new tests pass with a broken helper or a disabled Timer

A helper comparing only `getMinutes()` passes, since no case has the same minute in another hour, and so does a commented-out Timer, because the wiring check reads the raw file instead of the comment-stripped `widgetSource`.

**Suggested change:** Add a same-minute, earlier-hour case and run the wiring regex against `widgetSource`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (mutants pass at 4309fba)</summary>

# Reproducer: the new tests pass with a broken helper or a disabled Timer

Reviewed head: 4309fba052e951177628ba25e8546ff467d92b38. Each mutant is a
throwaway copy of the head. The test is the PR's `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh`,
unchanged.

## Mutant 1: the helper compares only the minute of the hour

`shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js`:

```js
function clockMinuteIsStale(shown, now) {
  return shown.getMinutes() !== now.getMinutes()
}
```

Result: `bash test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` exits 0 with every check `ok`, the
same 159 `ok` lines as the unmodified head. A label from 14:05 is then not
stale at 15:05:30, so a suspend of a whole number of hours (to within the
minute) would leave the old label up until SystemClock's delayed tick, up to a minute,
as before this PR.

This assertion catches it (it passes at the head):

```js
assert(calendar.clockMinuteIsStale(new Date(2026, 8, 27, 14, 5, 0), new Date(2026, 8, 27, 15, 5, 30)), 'clock sees a label from the same minute of an earlier hour as stale')
```

On the mutant: `not ok - clock sees a label from the same minute of an earlier hour as stale`

## Mutant 2: the whole catch-up Timer commented out

In `shell/plugins/panels/clock/BarWidget.qml`, each line from `Timer {` to its
closing `}` gets the prefix `// `.

Result: the PR's test still prints
`ok - clock checks for a stale minute and refreshes the label` and exits 0.
The new assertion reads `BarWidget.qml` raw (`clockWidget`) instead of the
file's `widgetSource`, which strips comment lines for this reason (lines 11–14
of the test).

The same regex run against `widgetSource` catches it (it passes at the head):

```js
assert(/Timer \{[^}]*running: !root\.showsSeconds[^}]*clockMinuteIsStale\(root\.displayDate, new Date\(\)\)\) root\.refresh\(\)/.test(widgetSource), 'clock checks for a stale minute in live (uncommented) code')
```

On the mutant: `not ok - clock checks for a stale minute in live (uncommented) code`

## Controls

- Deleting the Timer outright fails the PR's test:
  `not ok - clock checks for a stale minute and refreshes the label`.
- The PR's test run against the merge-base code fails with
  `TypeError: calendar.clockMinuteIsStale is not a function`, as the PR says.
- Also not pinned: `interval: 60000` passes the PR's test (minor).
</details>
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- After a resume the poll corrects a stale label within one 5 s poll (from source; no real suspend was run).
- The helper compares epoch minutes. Offsets were whole minutes in all 418 ICU zones on four 2026 dates, and a scan across DST changes in 9 zones (including +05:45 and Lord Howe's 30-minute shift) found no missed label change.
- The PR's tests fail on the base code and pass at the head.

**Optional notes**
- `refresh()` also calls the panel's `goToToday()`, so a calendar left open on another month jumps back to the current month after a resume in which the minute changed, and on a rolled-back minute (from source).
- In `Model.js`, the new function sits between `clockNeedsSeconds`'s doc comment and `clockNeedsSeconds`, which is now left without its comment.

**Related open PRs:** #12277, #13347 and #10138 fix the same problem in other ways and conflict with this PR in `BarWidget.qml`. #9509 and #13658 refresh the clock over IPC on wake; they touch other files.
</details>
